tasks.short: Develop final construction plans and aesthetic details.

steps.what: Develop final construction plans and their details.
Place details the architect already chose.
Review aesthetic representations of the structure.

tasks.design: Developing the final construction plans, including aesthetic representations and construction details, stays the architect's work on {OPS_SYSTEM}. A detail is placed only after it was chosen. The review of how the structure looks stays. A placed detail is not a new design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Final plans were redrawn from the design model, and an old detail was left in.
tasks.enabler_now: A chosen detail can be placed. Whether it is the right representation cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A detail that fights the aesthetic, or a plan that is not ready to be final, stays the development and the review.
tasks.human_edge: The architect sees a correct detail in the wrong composition.
tasks.altitude: Placing a chosen detail takes less redrawing. Developing the plans and reviewing the representation stay.

evidence.claim: Placing a detail that was already chosen is a copy. Developing the final plan is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the architect develops and reviews the final plans. Issuing them for construction is a different task.
Structured input: detail id, plan id, chosen or not. Producer is the architect. A detail that was not chosen is not placed.
Development time stays. The placement does not invent a representation.
unknowns: Who may call a plan final?
research_questions: How often is a final plan redrawn because a detail was out of date?

already_counted.description: Developing the plans is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire placed details when the plan revision changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If details are not stored, nothing is placed and the architect still develops the plans. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe construction on site against the plans.

steps.what: Open the plan items for this visit.
Conduct periodic observations of construction work.
Monitor compliance of that work with the plans.

tasks.design: Plan items for the visit open from {PROJECT}. Conducting periodic on-site observations stays on site. Monitoring compliance with the plans is the architect's note. A list of items is not an observation, and it does not instruct the contractor by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visits relied on memory of the drawings, and a departure was written up days later.
tasks.enabler_now: A plan item can be listed. Whether the work matches it cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Work that is covered up, or a departure the drawing does not settle, stays the observation.
tasks.human_edge: The architect can see work that meets the line and still is not the intent.
tasks.altitude: Opening the visit list takes less searching. The observation and the compliance note stay.

evidence.claim: A visit list from the plans is a query. An on-site observation is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the architect observes and notes compliance. Directing the contractor's means and methods is not this task. A formal instruction is a different task.
Structured input: plan item id, visit date, note. Producer is the plans for the list and the architect for the note. An item that was not seen is marked not observed.
Site time stays. The list does not mark work compliant.
unknowns: Are plan items identifiable on site?
research_questions: How often is a departure noticed only after the work is covered?

already_counted.description: The site observation is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire visit lists after the visit is written up.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If plan items are not listed, the visit is unchanged and the architect still observes. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult clients on functional and spatial requirements.

steps.what: Consult with clients about the structures.
File the requirements the architect determined.

tasks.design: Consulting the client stays a conversation. Determining functional and spatial requirements of the structures stays the architect's note. {PROJECT} files that determination. A room list is not inferred from the first remark.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were restated differently in each meeting note.
tasks.enabler_now: Filing a named requirement is a record. Determining it is not.
tasks.still_hard: A client who has not decided, or two uses that conflict, stays the consultation.
tasks.human_edge: The architect hears the use the client has not found words for.
tasks.altitude: Filing the agreed requirements takes less rewriting. The consultation and the determination stay.

evidence.claim: A requirements record stops a blank use. It does not hold the consultation.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the architect consults and determines the requirements. Designing the plan is a different task.
Structured input: project id, use, spatial note, functional note. Producer is the architect after the consultation. A requirement the architect has not determined is not filed.
Consultation time stays. The file does not add a use.
unknowns: Who confirms a requirement before design?
Are uses named the same way on every job?
research_questions: How often is a requirement rediscovered at a later meeting?

already_counted.description: The consultation is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire requirements when the brief is replaced.

approvals.approved_version: requirements the architect determined after that consultation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the client has not met, nothing is filed and the determination does not start. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Integrate engineering elements into one design.

steps.what: List clashes between the engineering elements.
Integrate engineering elements into unified designs.

tasks.design: Clashes between engineering elements are listed from the model on {OPS_SYSTEM} where the elements occupy the same place. Integrating them into one architectural design stays the architect. {PROJECT} records that design. A clash list is not a resolution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Engineering drawings arrived separately, and a clash was found on site.
tasks.enabler_now: Two elements in the same place can be listed. How to integrate them cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A clash the model does not show, or a resolution that hurts the design, stays the integration.
tasks.human_edge: The architect can choose which element moves without losing the intent.
tasks.altitude: Listing geometric clashes takes less overlaying. Integrating them into the design stays.

evidence.claim: Listing elements that occupy the same place is a check. The source pack names rule-based model checking. Resolving the design is not a measured case here.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the architect integrates the design. The engineers still own their calculations. This task does not change an engineer's signed calculation.
Structured input: element id, clash id, resolution. Producer is the model for the clash and the architect for the resolution. A clash is not deleted until a resolution is recorded.
Integration time stays. The list does not move an element.
unknowns: Are engineering elements in one model?
Who may move a structural element?
research_questions: How often is a clash found only on site?

already_counted.description: Integrating the design is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire clash lists when the model revision changes.

approvals.approved_version: unified design the architect integrated for that model

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the elements are not in one model, the list is empty and the architect still integrates from the drawings. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Final plans, site observations and client requirements stay with the architect. A chosen detail can be placed. A clash can be listed. The unified design is still a decision.
reach: The contractor hears a compliance note from the visit.
The client can read the requirements that were determined.
skills_to_grow: Do not mark work compliant because it was on the visit list.
Do not move an element just to clear a clash.
role.ambitious_version: A site departure is noted while it can still be seen, and a requirement is not rediscovered at the next meeting.
